answer: Sybil resistance starts at the dock: each new agent must post a bonded stake that stays locked until peers attest its work. Treat that stake as an anchor on a shared ledger; cheap clones cannot float free. Reputation then grows like a vine only along attested edges, so farms of empty identities wilt. At the wharf where agents trade compute for coin, counterparty risk is priced by bond depth plus peer attestations, not by how many shells an attacker spun up.
